closes: Adds normalized (locally-adaptive) nonconformity conformal prediction to the module UQ battery.
Closes the adaptive/normalized-nonconformity item left open by mondrian-conformal-openpoly-tg-v1 (does_not_close[3]).
Quantifies the efficiency/adaptivity/conditional-coverage trade of a variable-width band vs the constant-width band on OpenPoly Tg under a fully shared, non-circular protocol.
does_not_close: Does not establish wet-lab qualification, batch release, or human parity.
sigma(x) is a k-NN difficulty estimate; a model-based (MAD-fit, Lei 2018) or ensemble-variance sigma may differ. Not exhausted here.
Marginal validity is finite-sample distribution-free; exact per-point conditional coverage remains impossible distribution-free (Vovk 2012; Lei-Wasserman 2014).
Ridge base learner is a deterministic reference, not the module's production predictor.
OpenPoly Tg is a polymer benchmark used as a UQ-method testbed; it is NOT the DGEBA/amine coating target and carries no coating-property claim.

G4_normalized_band_is_nondegenerate.note: Passes iff widths vary; does NOT assert error-tracking (see Q3).

G5_label_permutation_control.note: sigma built from permuted proper-train residuals; real x<->difficulty signal removed. Real adaptivity should exceed permuted; marginal coverage retained.

headline: Normalized / locally-adaptive split-conformal prediction (Papadopoulos-Gammerman-Vovk 2008; Papadopoulos-Haralambous 2011; Lei et al. 2018; Bostrom-Johansson 2020) is added to the tolerance-robustness UQ battery, closing the adaptive-nonconformity gap left open by the signed Mondrian receipt. On OpenPoly experimental Tg (n=442) with the SAME fixed Ridge base learner, seed and 50/50 calibration split as the signed constant-width split-conformal method, a k-NN (k=15) label-free difficulty estimate sigma(x) turns the constant 165.4 K half-width into an adaptive band spanning [72.4, 338.4] K. Marginal coverage: ordinary 0.938 vs normalized 0.955 (guarantee floor 0.95). Median interval width: ordinary 330.8 K vs normalized 355.0 K (not tighter). Adaptivity: half-width-vs-abs-error Spearman rho=0.020, width CV=0.278. Difficulty-conditional worst tercile: ordinary 0.915 vs normalized 0.898. Two-replay byte-stable; 5/5 known-answer gates pass. AUDIT_ONLY; scientific_readiness stays LOCKED_INTERNAL/UNVALIDATED.
non_circularity: Ordinary constant-width and normalized split-conformal share ONE fixed base learner, seed, 60/40 pool/test split, 50/50 proper-train/calibration partition and test set (identical to the signed jackknife+/CV+ and Mondrian receipts). The ONLY difference is constant vs sigma(x)-normalized conformity. sigma(x) is a function of x and the frozen proper-train model alone (k-NN over proper-train abs-residuals); it never uses the calibration or test label, so split-conformal exchangeability and the finite-sample coverage guarantee are preserved. Target labels are experimental Tg from OpenPoly.

normalized_adaptive_conformal.theory: Papadopoulos-Haralambous 2011 / Lei et al. 2018 normalized nonconformity

protocol.difficulty_estimator: sigma(x) = beta + mean kNN(k=15) proper-train abs-residual; beta = mean proper-train abs-residual

purpose: Add normalized (locally-adaptive) nonconformity split-conformal prediction to the tolerance-robustness UQ battery and test whether a label-free difficulty rescaling sigma(x) converts the constant-width conformal band into an adaptive band that (a) retains marginal (1-alpha) coverage, (b) is more efficient (tighter median width), (c) is genuinely adaptive (width tracks error), and (d) improves difficulty-conditional coverage -- the relevant robustness property when a formulation lands in a hard, high-uncertainty regime that a single constant band under-covers.
theory_reference: Papadopoulos, Gammerman, Vovk 2008, Normalized nonconformity measures for regression Confidence Machines, COPA
Papadopoulos, Haralambous 2011, Reliable prediction intervals with regression neural networks, Neural Networks 24(8):842-851, doi:10.1016/j.neunet.2011.05.008

Bostrom, Johansson 2020, Mondrian conformal regressors, COPA, PMLR 128:114-133
